cf.title: Support EXCEPT for ALL SEQUENCES publications

input.subject: Support EXCEPT for ALL SEQUENCES publications

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection is fatal, and the feature extends the committed FOR ALL TABLES ... EXCEPT mechanism with pg_dump, psql and ALTER covered. Three fixable points remain. Demand rests on two reviewer +1s (demand-1). The subscriber's behaviour after an exclusion list changes is not documented (replication-ondisk-1). The choice to store sequences in pg_publication_rel was defended on lookup cost only (maintenance-fit-1). A committer who knows the publication catalog has to settle the last two.

brief.title: Support EXCEPT for ALL SEQUENCES publications
brief.problem: FOR ALL SEQUENCES publishes every persistent sequence, so a user cannot leave out one sequence. Reviewers named node-specific, temporary-purpose but persistent sequences that need no replication. The patch also aims to match the existing FOR ALL TABLES ... EXCEPT support.
brief.proposed_design: The patch adds an EXCEPT (SEQUENCE ...) clause to CREATE PUBLICATION and ALTER PUBLICATION ... SET ALL SEQUENCES. It stores excluded sequences in pg_publication_rel with prexcept set, next to excluded tables, so readers tell them apart by relkind. SET ALL SEQUENCES with EXCEPT replaces the exclusion list, and without EXCEPT it clears the list.
user_visible_surface: SQL: create publication ... for all sequences except (sequence s1, s2), also combined with all tables except (...).
SQL: alter publication ... set all sequences [except (sequence ...)] replaces or clears sequence exclusions.
Catalog: pg_publication_rel.prrelid and prexcept now also cover sequences; prattrs and prqual are always null for sequences.
psql: \dRp+ shows an "Except sequences:" footer, and \d+ on a sequence lists publications that exclude it.
pg_dump emits the EXCEPT (SEQUENCE ...) clause in CREATE PUBLICATION, and psql tab completion covers the new syntax.
author_claims: The change brings sequence publications in line with FOR ALL TABLES ... EXCEPT.
Excluded sequences are not sent to the subscriber.
An exclusion follows the sequence across rename and ALTER SEQUENCE ... SET SCHEMA.
A sequence excluded by one publication but included by another in the same subscription is replicated.
Storing sequences in pg_publication_rel adds no meaningful cost, because relkind lookups are cached on hot paths.
brief.thread_state: Peter Smith, shveta malik, vignesh C, Ashutosh Sharma and Zsolt Parragi reviewed through v28, and solai v tested v11 without finding problems. shveta reported no further comments at v24; the patch has since been only rebased and fixed after rebase errors, and no committer has replied.
unclear: The thread shows no committer view on storing sequences in pg_publication_rel instead of a separate catalog, which Peter Smith questioned.
The material does not say if the subscriber needs ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION after the exclusion list changes; only a test fix implies it.
Shlok's offer to check relkind in OpenRelationList, which would avoid separate table and sequence lists in ALTER, got no answer.
The temporary-sequence error now names a backend-specific schema like pg_temp_2; the thread does not decide between redacting it in tests and using get_namespace_name_or_temp.

prior_attempts.title: Skip replicating the tables specified in except table option
prior_attempts.quote: As I did not see much interest from others, I'm withdrawing this patch for now.
prior_attempts.reason: The author withdrew the patch after the thread went quiet. From mid-2022 the messages are rebases and commitfest reminders, and the author said he saw little interest from others. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut doubted the feature was worth the trouble and pointed to the cost of tracking negative dependencies. Peter Smith found the meaning of ALTER PUBLICATION combined with EXCEPT ambiguous, but these points did not decide the outcome.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 proposed EXCEPT TABLE for FOR ALL TABLES. Message #1 reports that the table version has since been committed, and this proposal extends the same mechanism to FOR ALL SEQUENCES.

objections.title: Use case for excluding sequences is stated but not shown
objections.failure_scenario: The project adds EXCEPT (SEQUENCE ...) syntax and starts storing sequences in pg_publication_rel, and pg_dump, psql and later publication patches must handle them. If few users ever exclude a sequence, that cost stays and buys little. The proposal does not say what goes wrong today when a node-local sequence is synchronized anyway.
objections.argument: The only demand in the thread is two reviewer +1s describing a general case: temporary-purpose but persistent, node-specific sequences (messages #2, #3). There is no field report, no -general or -bugs thread, and no description of the harm, such as a subscriber error or an overwritten value. Symmetry with ALL TABLES EXCEPT (message #1) is the main argument, and it lowers the cost of the feature but does not show users need it. An earlier EXCEPT TABLE proposal was withdrawn for lack of interest [P3], but EXCEPT TABLE has since gone in, so that precedent weighs little here.
objections.author_must_show: What concrete failure or cost do users hit today when FOR ALL SEQUENCES synchronizes a node-local sequence, and is there a user report of it?

precedents.title: Skip replicating the tables specified in except table option

critic.reasoning: The thread shows two reviewer +1s with a general use case and no user report or described harm. P3 must not be used as support, because EXCEPT for ALL TABLES was committed later; the fitting outcome is "show demand".

objections.title: Subscriber state after changing a sequence exclusion list is undefined
objections.failure_scenario: An administrator runs alter publication ... set all sequences except (sequence s1) because s1 is node-local. The subscriber still lists s1 in pg_subscription_rel. A later alter subscription ... refresh sequences may overwrite the local s1 value, and the administrator finds out only when the subscriber's s1 hands out values that clash with local use.
objections.argument: Message #62 shows the TAP test failed until alter subscription ... refresh publication was added, so the subscriber's pg_subscription_rel keeps an excluded sequence until that command runs. The documentation hunks for alter_publication.sgml and logical-replication.sgml do not tell users to run it, or what refresh sequences does in the meantime. Message #54 asked for this flow to be tested, but the material shows no answer on what users must do.
objections.author_must_show: After set all sequences except adds a sequence, what does refresh sequences do on the subscriber before refresh publication runs, and where is the required step documented?

critic.reasoning: Message #62 shows the subscriber keeps the excluded sequence until REFRESH PUBLICATION runs. The shown documentation hunks do not say this, or what REFRESH SEQUENCES does before then, so I could not refute it.

objections.title: Mixed tables and sequences in pg_publication_rel rely on unchecked invariants
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds FOR SEQUENCE s1, so a publication can include some sequences and exclude others. Existing readers assume that any sequence row for an ALL SEQUENCES publication is an exclusion. They will then treat included sequences as excluded, or the reverse. Nothing fails at build or test time; users find out when subscriber sequence values are wrong.
objections.argument: Peter Smith (message #9) listed the row combinations that now exist and asked why sequences share the catalog. The answer in messages #14 and #19 covered lookup cost, which is a different concern. Several readers depend on implicit rules: psql omits the prexcept check (messages #31, #39), GetIncludedPublicationRelations returns an empty list for ALL SEQUENCES (messages #66, #67), and get_delete_rels must be called per relkind (message #72). The idea in message #72 to check relkind once in OpenRelationList got no reply.
objections.author_must_show: Which mechanism makes a future reader of pg_publication_rel fail visibly if it forgets the relkind or prexcept filter, for example once FOR SEQUENCE exists?

critic.reasoning: Messages #14 and #19 answered Peter Smith's catalog question on lookup cost only, and no committer has weighed in. The FOR SEQUENCE scenario is hypothetical, but message #9 names it and nothing shown makes a reader fail visibly.

refuted.title: Excluded sequences change what existing pg_publication_rel queries return
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring script written for Postgres 19 lists excluded tables with `select prrelid::regclass from pg_publication_rel where prexcept`. After upgrade to 20, the same query also returns excluded sequences, and the script reports sequences as excluded tables. The operator finds out only when the report is compared against the publication definition.
refuted.argument: In Postgres 19, rows with prexcept set are only tables, so external tools can rely on that without a relkind join. Message #9 named this change in meaning, and the reply in message #14 covered cost and the C code inside Postgres. Clients outside the tree were not discussed. Older psql binaries reading a newer server may have the same gap, because the new relkind filters in describe.c exist only in the new client.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing client queries against pg_publication_rel, including older psql versions, would misread excluded sequences, and should the release notes or the catalog docs warn about it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2, which states the same catalog-reader concern and is judged there.

refuted.title: Subscriber does not show when a changed exclusion list takes effect
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator runs `alter publication p set all sequences except (sequence s1)` and then `alter subscription ... refresh sequences`, expecting s1 to stop syncing. The subscriber still has s1 in pg_subscription_rel and keeps overwriting the local sequence. The operator finds out when the node-local values are lost.
refuted.argument: Message #62 shows that a test failed until `ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION` was added after the exclusion list changed. The documentation hunks for ALTER PUBLICATION do not say this. Sequences have a separate REFRESH SEQUENCES command that a user may reasonably think is enough. The stated use case in message #3 is sequences that are local to one node, which makes this the case where a silent overwrite matters most.
refuted.author_must_show: What does REFRESH SEQUENCES do with a sequence that was newly excluded, and will the ALTER PUBLICATION docs say that REFRESH PUBLICATION is required?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which hedges the overwrite claim where this one states it as fact.

refuted.title: Existing readers of prexcept rows will now also see sequences
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring query written for Postgres 19 lists excluded tables with a pg_publication_rel join on prexcept, with no relkind filter, because only tables could appear there. On Postgres 20, for a publication defined as both all tables and all sequences, it reports excluded sequences as excluded tables. An older psql running \dRp+ against a 20 server may do the same.
refuted.argument: Message #9 noted that a row's meaning now depends on the relkind of prrelid. Messages #14 and #15 answered this for C hot paths only, not for SQL readers of the catalog. The catalogs.sgml hunk changes prrelid to "table or sequence" but has no compatibility note. The thread shows no committer view on this, so the cost to external tools has not been weighed against a separate catalog.
refuted.author_must_show: Which existing SQL readers of pg_publication_rel prexcept rows, including older psql \dRp+, give wrong output on a server with excluded sequences, and how are they warned?

critic.reasoning: Postgres does not promise stable catalog contents across major versions, and psql does not support newer servers. The catalogs.sgml hunk documents the new meaning of prrelid and prexcept, as Postgres 19 did when prexcept rows first appeared.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The exclusion list changes which sequences logical replication synchronizes to the subscriber.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: pg_publication_rel.prrelid and prexcept now also cover sequences, so readers tell rows apart by relkind.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The patch changes pg_publication.h and parsenodes.h, which extensions that read publications compile against.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: gram.y gains EXCEPT (SEQUENCE ...) for CREATE PUBLICATION and ALTER PUBLICATION ... SET ALL SEQUENCES.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump must emit the EXCEPT (SEQUENCE ...) clause in CREATE PUBLICATION.

touch_points.label: psql UX conventions
touch_points.reason: \dRp+ gains an "Except sequences:" footer, \d+ on a sequence lists excluding publications, and tab completion changes.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every later reader of pg_publication_rel must filter by relkind and prexcept, and nothing fails visibly if one does not.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Publication membership checks now need relkind lookups; the author says these are cached on hot paths.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: After SET ALL SEQUENCES EXCEPT adds a sequence, what does ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH SEQUENCES do on the subscriber before REFRESH PUBLICATION runs?
Will the ALTER PUBLICATION documentation say that the subscriber needs REFRESH PUBLICATION after the exclusion list changes?
What makes a future reader of pg_publication_rel fail visibly if it omits the relkind or prexcept filter, for example once FOR SEQUENCE exists?
What concrete failure or cost do users hit today when FOR ALL SEQUENCES synchronizes a node-local sequence, and is there a user report of it?
Will OpenRelationList check relkind once, as message #72 offered, so that ALTER does not need separate table and sequence lists?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows the publication catalog and logical replication of sequences. No committer has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the meaning of sequence rows in pg_publication_rel, the new syntax, and the pg_dump and psql output. All of these stay for every later release and constrain a future FOR SEQUENCE design.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered reviews and rebased the series through v28 over seven months, which suggests continued follow-up.

priority.reason: Reviewers reported no further comments at v24 and the patch has only been rebased since, with no committer reply. The feature serves users with node-local persistent sequences, and it adds syntax and mixed-relkind catalog rows across the parser, the catalog code, pg_dump and psql.

provisional_note: The code was not read, so the handling of relkind and prexcept filters in each reader of pg_publication_rel could not be checked. The subscriber's behaviour between ALTER PUBLICATION and REFRESH PUBLICATION is inferred from a test fix in message #62.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: logical decoding and replication of sequences, take 2
precedents_retrieved.summary: Extend logical decoding with a sequence callback, and extend built-in logical replication so publications can include sequences, so that a logical replica's sequences track the primary and do not produce duplicate values after failover. Sequence increments were decoded non-transactionally by default, and transactionally when the sequence's relfilenode was created or altered in an in-progress transaction.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why the 2024 'take 2' entry was withdrawn. They do show that an earlier committed version was reverted in April 2022. Review had found that non-transactional sequence changes could be discarded or hit an assertion before the decoding snapshot was consistent, and mixing transactional and non-transactional decoding caused snapshot, abort and streaming problems. The author judged that a fix would need an extensive redesign that was too late for that release cycle, and posted an alternative that WAL-logs sequence state at commit time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The approach combining transactional and non-transactional behavior implemented by the patch clearly has issues, and it seems foolish to hope we'll find a simple fix.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip replicating the tables specified in except table option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an EXCEPT TABLE clause to CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION ... FOR ALL TABLES, which records excluded tables in pg_publication_rel and makes pgoutput skip their changes. A companion patch adds ALTER PUBLICATION ... RESET, which returns a publication to its default state before ALL TABLES with an exception list is added.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after the thread went quiet. From mid-2022 the messages are rebases and commitfest reminders, and the author said he saw little interest from others. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut doubted the feature was worth the trouble and pointed to the cost of tracking negative dependencies. Peter Smith found the meaning of ALTER PUBLICATION combined with EXCEPT ambiguous, but these points did not decide the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As I did not see much interest from others, I'm withdrawing this patch
for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve pg_dump dumping publication tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes pg_dump's getPublicationTables() to fetch all publication-table memberships with a single query, instead of iterating over every table and issuing a separate query per table. The matching TableInfo for each row is then looked up in tblinfoindex, which should be faster when there are many tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch was superseded, not rejected: Tom Lane had already committed practically the same change in passing (commit 8e396a773), which also removed the server-side join. He therefore marked the entry withdrawn. Cary Huang's earlier concern about client-side memory use with very many publication tables was answered by Tom Lane as not significant compared to the per-table data pg_dump already collects.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'll mark this CF entry "withdrawn", since it wasn't rejected
exactly.  Too bad we don't have a classification of "superseded
by events", or something like that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop."
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop."
Reverted commit(s): pg_createsubscriber: Add log message when no publications exist to drop.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 74ac377d75135e02064fc4427bec401277b4f60c.

The previous change contained a misconception about how publications
are cleaned up on the subscriber. The newly added log message could
confuse users, particularly when running pg_createsubscriber with
--dry-run - users would see a "dropping publication" message
immediately followed by a "no publications found" message.

precedents_retrieved.title: rich constructor for plpy.Error class, possible raise structured exception
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Catalin Iacob, Robert Haas, Alvaro Herrera
precedents_retrieved.summary: Pavel Stehule first proposed a plpy.ereport() function so PL/Python code could raise errors with every ereport field (detail, hint, sqlstate and others). After review the design moved to keyword arguments on the plpy exception constructors and then to new plpy.raise_* functions next to the existing plpy.info, plpy.error and similar functions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Author and reviewer did not agree on the interface. Catalin Iacob preferred changing plpy.error and friends to accept detail and hint, accepting a compatibility break, while Pavel Stehule's patch added parallel raise_* functions; Pavel then said the raise_* functions make no sense if compatibility is broken. Robert Haas and Alvaro Herrera said the two should reach consensus before a committer would take the patch. Open fixes also remained (raise Error rather than SPIError, merge the docs patch), and the author was out of office.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Actually I imagine that if there's no agreement between author and first reviewer, there might not *be* a committer in the first place.

precedents_retrieved.title: Optimize walsender handling invalid messages of 'drop publication'
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes how walsender handles invalidation messages from 'drop publication' on releases before PG 14, which lack the XLOG_XACT_INVALIDATIONS record type. pgoutput stops doing needless cache invalidation, and a relid-to-relfilenode hash map replaces a hash sequential search; the patch targets REL_13_STABLE and back branches only.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No one reviewed the patch for four months. Andres Freund then objected that users hitting the issue should upgrade, and that performance improvements are rarely backpatched, and not when they would go only into back branches without first maturing in the development branch. The author later withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's one thing to decide to backpatch an
optimization if it had time to "mature" in the development branch, but from
what I undestand you're proposing to apply this just to the back branches.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply worker fails if a relation is missing on subscriber even if refresh publication has not been refreshed yet
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch would let the logical replication apply worker skip changes for tables that were added to a publication but are not yet in pg_subscription_rel on the subscriber, because ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... REFRESH PUBLICATION has not been run. It would log a warning instead of failing repeatedly when such a table is missing on the subscriber.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Amit Kapila questioned whether the current ERROR behavior should be changed when no specific use case had been given. He noted that users can avoid the failure loop with the disable_on_error subscription parameter, and that silently skipping changes could surprise users whose subscriber-side setup is incomplete. The author said he had no specific use case, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I see your point but not sure if it is worth changing the
current behavior without any specific use case which we want to
address with this change.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical replication timeout
precedents_retrieved.summary: A walsender spent hours unlinking every possible spill file name for a large transaction in ReorderBufferRestoreCleanup, so the subscriber timed out and decoding restarted in a loop. The patch records which WAL segments a transaction actually spilled to, so cleanup removes only those files.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last shown message, in March 2025, only reports a rebase. A reviewer had also asked for a second patch that sends progress updates during long loops such as cleanup, and no message shows that patch.

roaster_notes.note: P3 died for lack of interest, and its doubts about negative dependencies came up in an AI summary only. Both points have lost weight since the table version of EXCEPT was committed, and here several reviewers back the sequence extension (messages #2, #3, #15). The thread cites no other earlier attempt.
The syntax follows the existing FOR ALL TABLES EXCEPT form. pg_dump, psql describe output and tab completion are covered, so no objection is raised on those points.
Nothing changes WAL, on-disk relation formats or the wire protocol; the catalog has no new columns, so pg_upgrade only needs pg_dump to emit the new except (sequence ...) clause.

The proposal adds no new privilege path. FOR ALL SEQUENCES publications, and changes to them, already need superuser, and an exclusion only reduces what gets sent. The new psql queries read pg_publication_rel, which is already readable by all users. The pg_temp_N schema name in the new error message exposes nothing a session cannot already see.
The hot-path cost was weighed in message #14 and seems small. Shared EXCEPT syntax copies committed practice for tables. No committer has engaged, which affects committability, not the merits.

Postgres has no existing way to drop one persistent sequence from a FOR ALL SEQUENCES publication. Per-sequence FOR SEQUENCE does not exist (message #9), and making a sequence unlogged to exclude it changes its crash behaviour, so that is no substitute. The patch reuses the FOR ALL TABLES ... EXCEPT mechanism and pg_publication_rel, so it does not add a second mechanism. No extension can change publication membership.
Demand is thin but the feature copies existing ALL TABLES EXCEPT practice and its cost falls mostly on its users, so the objection is 'show demand', not rejection.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (demand-1); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
